Confidential | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-01
THIS AGREEMENT is dated 2034-09-27 and is made between:
(1) Quillmere Pharma Inc., whose principal office is at 315 Linden Parade, Suite 775, Fallowmere 26170, USA (the Shipper);
and
(2) Tarrowby Express Inc., whose principal office is at 214 Merrow Road, Suite 671, Fallowmere 20905, USA (the Carrier).
Recitals
(A) WHEREAS the Carrier provides express air transport and related handling, storage, delivery and customs services;
(B) WHEREAS the Shipper wishes to engage the Carrier to provide those services for its shipments; and
(C) WHEREAS the parties wish to record the terms on which the Carrier provides those services.
NOW THEREFORE the parties agree as follows.
1 Definitions. In this Agreement the following terms have the meanings below.
1.1 Qualifying Spend. Qualifying Spend means freight charges (base freight, fuel, security surcharge and Annex D
accessorials) on invoices dated in the period, net of all credit notes dated in the period whatever invoice they reference (rebate
and improvement credits excepted). It excludes taxes (sales tax, GST), duties and disbursements, late fees, and rebate or
improvement credits. INR amounts are converted per invoice at the Annex F rate for the month of the invoice date.
1.2 Pickup Date. Pickup Date means the date the Carrier takes possession, as recorded in the Carrier's tracking record.
1.3 Authorised Person. Authorised Person means a person listed in Schedule 1 for the relevant category.
1.4 Contract Year. Contract Year means each 12-month period starting on the Effective Date or an anniversary of it.
1.5 Quarter. Quarter means a calendar quarter.
2 Term
2.1 Effective date. This Agreement takes effect on 2034-10-20 (the Effective Date).
2.2 Initial term. The initial term is 12 months, ending on 2035-10-19.
2.3 Auto-renewal. This Agreement does not renew automatically. It ends at the end of the initial term unless extended under
clause 2.4.
2.4 Extension. The term may be extended only by an instrument signed by both parties.
3 Rates and charges
3.1 Rates. Services are charged at the rates in Annex A (express air). Period 2 rates continue to apply after month 12 of the term
(including any renewal or extension) until an amendment replaces them.
3.2 Pricing date. Each shipment is priced at the rates, surcharges and fees in force on its Pickup Date.
3.3 Chargeable weight. Chargeable weight is the greater of actual and volumetric weight (L x W x H cm / 6000), rounded up to
the next 0.5 kg.
3.4 Minimum charge. The per-shipment minimum in Annex A applies where rate x chargeable weight is lower. Each shipment
is rated at the weight band that contains its chargeable weight.
3.5 Rate notices. The Carrier may change Annex A rates by written notice from an Authorised Person (rates), effective on the
date stated in the notice.
4 Surcharges
4.1 Fuel surcharge. Fuel surcharge is the Annex C percentage for the month of the Pickup Date, applied to the base freight
charge only. It does not apply to Annex D accessorials or the security surcharge.
4.2 Security surcharge. Security surcharge is charged per chargeable kg at the Annex D rate.
5 Dangerous goods and dry ice
5.1 Dangerous goods fee. Shipments requiring a dangerous goods declaration attract the DG Fee in Annex D, once per
shipment.
5.2 Dry ice. Dry ice (UN1845) used solely as a refrigerant for non-dangerous goods is billed at the Dry Ice Handling Fee in
Annex D, once per shipment (not per package or per kg), and does not attract the Dangerous Goods Fee.

5.3 Mixed shipments. Where a shipment contains dangerous goods other than dry ice, only the DG Fee applies (not both).
6 Storage, delivery and customs
6.1 Storage. Storage days = release date - arrival date (ARRIVED_FACILITY) - 5 free days, minimum 0. The arrival day
counts; the release day (DELIVERED or COLLECTED_BY_CONSIGNEE) is not charged. Storage charge = storage days x the
Annex D rate. Example: arrived 10 Mar, released 17 Mar, 5 free days: 17 - 10 - 5 = 2 days charged.
6.2 Delivery. The delivery fee is payable only where the Carrier performs delivery to the consignee's address.
6.3 Customs holds. Customs hold and examination fees are for the Shipper's account, except where the hold results from an
error or omission in documents prepared or filed by the Carrier.
7 Volume rebate
7.1 Volume rebate. The Carrier shall credit a rebate on each Quarter's Qualifying Spend (QS) at the tier reached: QS >= USD
79,000.00: 5%; QS >= USD 120,000.00: 7.5%; QS >= USD 202,000.00: 10%. The tier rate applies to all QS in the Quarter.
7.2 Thresholds. Rebate thresholds are in USD per Quarter.
7.3 Rebate credit. Rebate credit notes are issued within 45 days after Quarter end.
8 Handling margin
8.1 Handling margin. Not applicable to this Agreement.
8.2 Margin step-down. Not applicable to this Agreement.
9 Annual improvement credit
9.1 Annual improvement credit. Within 60 days after each anniversary of the Effective Date, the Carrier shall issue a credit of
1.42% of the prior Contract Year's Qualifying Spend.
10 Payment
10.1 Payment terms. Invoices are due 45 days after the invoice date.
10.2 Late fee. Undisputed amounts unpaid more than 0 days after the due date bear a late fee of 1.98% per month or part
thereof. days_late = paid date - due date; no fee is due if days_late <= 0; otherwise n = ceil(days_late / 30) fee months, each
fee_i = 1.98% x base_i rounded to cents, base_i per clause 10.3.
10.3 Compounding. Late fees unpaid at the end of a month are added to the overdue balance, and the next month's fee is
charged on principal plus unpaid prior late fees. Fees shown paid leave the base.
10.4 Disputed amounts. No late fee accrues on amounts disputed in good faith under clause 13 while the dispute is open.
10.5 Extension of due date. A due date may be extended by written notice from the Carrier's Authorised Person (payment
terms); the extended date replaces the due date for clause 10.2.
11 Waivers
11.1 Waiver authority. A charge may be waived only in writing by a person listed in Schedule 1 for waivers. Schedule 1 is
exhaustive.
11.2 Scope of waiver. A waiver applies only to the charges and shipments it names. No waiver is a waiver of any later charge,
and no course of dealing creates one.
11.3 Conditional waiver. A waiver stated to be conditional takes effect only when the condition is met.
12 Notices and Schedule 1. Schedule 1 lists each party's Authorised Persons with categories (rates, waivers, payment_terms,
notices [the Key Account Manager], billing_disputes, treasury) and email addresses. Notices are effective only from and to
those addresses.
13 Billing disputes
13.1 Disputes. Billing disputes are raised with the Carrier's billing_disputes contact within 90 days of the invoice date.
13.2 Dispute notice. A dispute notice names the invoice, the charge and the amount disputed. The undisputed balance of the
invoice remains payable by its due date.

13.3 Unranked instruments. Where a rate notice under clause 3.5 and an amendment state different rates for the same lane and
period, the parties shall resolve the difference jointly; neither prevails automatically.
14 Precedence
14.1 Precedence. Signed amendment > this Agreement > Annexes. Between amendments, the later effective date prevails for
the terms it changes.
14.2 Correspondence. This clause does not rank correspondence against amendments (see clause 13.3).
14.3 Quoted text. Quoted or forwarded text is not a notice.
15 Scope of services and service levels
15.1 Services. The Carrier shall provide express air transport of documents and goods and related handling, storage, delivery
and customs services (the Services) for shipments tendered by the Shipper and its group companies, with the skill and care of a
competent carrier.
15.2 Service levels. The operations contacts of the parties shall agree transit-time targets for each lane in writing and review
performance against them each Quarter. Service levels are operational targets and are not pricing terms.
15.3 Shipper obligations. The Shipper shall describe, pack and mark each shipment accurately, and shall provide the
documents that applicable export, import and security rules require.
15.4 Subcontracting. The Carrier may use subcontractors and agents to perform the Services and remains responsible for their
performance.
16 Temperature-controlled shipments
16.1 Temperature ranges. Where the Shipper's booking instructions state a temperature range for a shipment, the Carrier shall
handle, store and transport it within that range, following the packaging and handling instructions the Shipper provides.
16.2 Good Distribution Practice. The Carrier shall maintain a quality system consistent with Good Distribution Practice for
medicinal products, including qualified facilities, trained staff, calibrated temperature monitoring and records of deviations, and
shall make those records available to the Shipper for audit on reasonable request.
16.3 Deviations. The Carrier shall inform the Shipper's operations team promptly of any temperature excursion or other
deviation affecting a shipment, and shall follow the Shipper's reasonable instructions to protect the goods.
17 Liability
17.1 Limit of liability. The Carrier's liability for destruction, loss of, damage to or delay in the carriage of a shipment is
governed by the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules for International Carriage by Air, Montreal, 28 May 1999 (the
Montreal Convention) where it applies. Liability is limited to 26 Special Drawing Rights (SDR) per kilogram of the gross
weight of the shipment or package concerned, unless the Shipper made a special declaration of interest in delivery at the time
the shipment was handed over.
17.2 Carriage outside the Convention. Where the Montreal Convention does not apply, the same limit of 26 SDR per kilogram
applies to the Carrier's liability, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
17.3 Exclusions. Neither party is liable for loss of profit, loss of business or market, or any indirect or consequential loss,
however caused.
17.4 Unlimited liability. Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud,
or for any liability that cannot be limited by law.
18 Cargo claims
18.1 Scope. This clause applies to claims for loss of, damage to or delay of goods. It does not apply to billing disputes, which
are governed by clause 13 only.
18.2 Damage. A claim for damage must be made in writing within 14 days from the date of receipt of the goods.
18.3 Delay. A claim for delay must be made in writing within 21 days from the date on which the goods were placed at the
consignee's disposal.
18.4 Loss. A claim for loss or non-delivery must be made in writing within 120 days from the date of issue of the air waybill.

18.5 Time bar. The right to damages is extinguished if an action is not brought within two years from the date of arrival at
destination, or the date on which the goods ought to have arrived.
19 Insurance
19.1 Carrier insurance. The Carrier shall maintain cargo legal liability insurance and general liability insurance with reputable
insurers, each for not less than USD 5,000,000.00 per occurrence, and shall provide certificates of insurance on request.
19.2 Cargo value. The Carrier does not insure the Shipper's goods. The Shipper may insure its goods for their full value at its
own cost.
20 Confidentiality
20.1 Confidential information. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and any information of the other
party marked or reasonably understood to be confidential, and shall use it only to perform this Agreement.
20.2 Exceptions. Clause 20.1 does not apply to information that is public other than through a breach of this clause, or that a
party must disclose by law, regulation or order of a competent authority, or to its professional advisers and auditors under a duty
of confidence.
20.3 Duration. This clause 20 survives for three years after this Agreement ends.
21 Data protection
21.1 Personal data. Each party shall process personal data received from the other party (such as consignee names, addresses
and contact details) only to perform the Services and in accordance with applicable data protection law.
21.2 Security. Each party shall keep such personal data secure against unauthorised access and shall notify the other party
without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach affecting it.
22 Compliance
22.1 Anti-bribery. Each party shall comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and shall not offer, give or
accept any bribe or improper payment in connection with this Agreement.
22.2 Sanctions and export control. Each party shall comply with applicable sanctions, export control and customs laws.
Neither party is required to perform any act that would breach them.
23 Force majeure
23.1 Relief. Neither party is liable for failure or delay in performing an obligation, other than an obligation to pay money, to the
extent caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, epidemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest,
government action, airport or airspace closure, and strikes not limited to the affected party's own staff.
23.2 Mitigation. The affected party shall notify the other party promptly, use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of the
event, and resume performance as soon as reasonably possible.
24 Termination
24.1 Termination for cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect if the other
party commits a material breach that is not remedied within 30 days after written notice of it, or becomes insolvent or enters into
an arrangement with its creditors.
24.2 Termination for convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by written notice that states
that it is given under this clause 24.2 and gives at least 90 days' notice of the termination date.
24.3 Term not affected. Subject to termination under this clause 24, clause 2 governs the duration of this Agreement. A notice
that is not expressly given under this clause 24 does not terminate this Agreement.
24.4 Effect of termination. Termination does not affect rights and obligations accrued before it takes effect, including amounts
payable for Services performed before that date.
25 Governing law and dispute resolution
25.1 Governing law. This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State
of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules.

25.2 Escalation. A dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, other than a billing dispute handled under clause
13, shall first be referred to a senior manager of each party.
25.3 Arbitration. A dispute that the senior managers do not resolve shall be finally resolved by arbitration administered by the
International Centre for Dispute Resolution under its International Arbitration Rules by a sole arbitrator. The seat of arbitration
is New York, New York. The language of the arbitration is English.
26 Assignment
26.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any right under it without the prior written consent of
the other party, except to a group company that takes over the relevant business, on written notice.
27 Entire agreement, counterparts and variation
27.1 Entire agreement. This Agreement, with its Annexes and Schedule 1, sets out the whole agreement of the parties on its
subject matter and supersedes all proposals, quotations and negotiations about it made before its date.
27.2 Variation. Except where this Agreement provides otherwise (including clauses 3.5, 10.5 and 11), a variation of this
Agreement is effective only if it is made in writing and signed by both parties.
27.3 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of
which is an original and which together are one instrument.
27.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the other provisions remain in force.
27.5 Third parties. No person other than the parties has any right to enforce any term of this Agreement.
Execution
IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have executed this Agreement by their duly authorised representatives on the date stated
on the cover page.
Executed by duly authorised officers. Schedule 1 governs Authorised Persons for rates, waivers, payment terms and notices.
